components.description: The rocket trail used for trajectories, horizons, the index and orbits.
components.css: .ds-trail { width: 320px; height: 60px; overflow: visible; } .ds-trail path { fill: none; stroke: rgb(245 241 250 / 0.42); stroke-width: 1.75; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-dasharray: 1 9; }

narrative.overview:
Every page is an entry in a log kept after landing on Jupiter: a precise, dated record of what was built and why, written by someone who stayed curious after arriving. The log is editorial first — large type, generous space, one idea per screen — and technical in its marginalia: file paths as eyebrows, line numbers, a `mission` object, code in the hero's palette. The planet and its sky give the record a place; they never stand between the visitor and the work.

The world is dark only. A night-side graphite ground carries everything; the plum of the upper atmosphere appears where projects live, reached gradually rather than through a hard band. Colour is scarce on purpose: lavender marks what you can act on, Jupiter's peach adds warmth in small doses, and the rest is graphite and starlight. Character lives in recurring details — the rocket's dotted trail, the ◆ that marks where you are, the code-path labels — so components themselves can stay precise and calm.

Motion is a single, deliberate moment per surface (the rocket's arrival, the slow orbit of a gallery) plus transitions that answer the visitor's actions. Everything respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the content is complete before any effect runs.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, graphite ground with a gradual plum atmosphere where projects live.
One action colour (lavender); peach only as a warm accent and for focus.
Manrope for reading, JetBrains Mono for anything that is code, data or a path.
Thin outlines and soft radii; depth from tone and soft violet glows, not stacked shadows.
The rocket's dotted trail as the system's recurring line: trajectory, horizon, index, orbit.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Lavender means "you can act on this". It is never a background wash, a decorative fill or body text; if an element is not interactive and is not the current location, it is not lavender.

rules.name: The Gradual Atmosphere Rule
rules.body: Plum is never a shaped band with an edge. It appears through a long gradient from graphite (about 28rem) and leaves the same way, so no seam can show.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks what a machine would print: paths, code, counts, codes, labels. It is never used for sentences.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Caps Rule
rules.body: Section eyebrows are lowercase code paths (`~/work`, `portfolio / work / yrest.mdoc`), never tracked uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Scene-Only Elevation Rule
rules.body: Only things that float in the sky get a glow or a shadow. Cards, buttons and blocks in the reading flow stay flat and rely on borders and tone.

dos: Do keep lavender for actions, the current location and the hero's highlighted word only.
Do use the dotted trail (1.75px dots every 10px, Starlight at 42%) for any trajectory, horizon, orbit or progress line.
Do label sections with a lowercase code path, and use mono for paths, code, counts and labels.
Do reach the plum surface through a long gradient from graphite and leave it the same way.
Do make every scene element decorative and hidden from assistive technology, and keep the content complete without JavaScript and with reduced motion.
donts: Don't use blurred bands, hard horizontal cuts or shaped colour blocks between sections; they showed seams at the screen edges.
Don't give cards, buttons or reading blocks a drop shadow; only floating scene objects get glow and shadow.
Don't use tracked uppercase eyebrow labels or numbered markers on content that is not a real sequence.
Don't add spatial jargon to navigation labels (Work, About, Contact stay plain), military imagery, game-like interfaces or omnipresent neon.
Don't let two pages overlap during a transition; the old page leaves before the new one arrives.
